newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cable & Wireless quits German venture.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless quits German venture.

text.p: Britain's Cable & Wireless hung up on Germany's Veba AG on Friday, confirming its long-anticipated departure from a German telephone venture with the utility.
Veba and its remaining German partner, utility RWE AG, forged ahead with a purely domestic telecommunications alliance.
The German Cartel Office in Berlin approved the domestic joint venture, to be called O.TEL.O, after it became clear Cable & Wireless would leave the alliance.

The departure of Cable & Wireless leaves the partnership formerly known as Vebacom without an international partner. Industry analysts said this could slow Veba's efforts to become a serious challenger to monopoly Deutsche Telekom.
Meanwhile, Britain's second-biggest telecommunications company denied it was effectively pulling out of Europe, even if it expected no imminent link-up with a global alliance.

Cable & Wireless has been viewed as the perfect partner for Global One -- marriage of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Kansas City, Mo.-based Sprint Corp. -- because it has access to two key markets Global One lacks -- Britain and Asia.
But C&W, whose Chief Executive Richard Brown is a former Sprint executive, said a deal with Global One or any other such alliance looked some way off.

Veba has agreed to pay Cable & Wireless about 2.21 billion marks ($1.3 billion) for the British company's 45 percent stake in the venture they formed two years ago. RWE joined the alliance last October but had no equity in the group because final contracts were not signed.

Veba chief Ulrich Hartmann, in an apparent reference to Cable & Wireless's reluctance to step up investment in telecommunications infrastructure in Germany, shrugged off the company's departure and said Veba and RWE were looking for a new partner.

"For our aggressive market strategy in Germany we need partners who can maintain our tempo," he said in a statement. "With RWE we have found a teammate who will work with the same strength and commitment toward our demanding goals."
RWE Chief Executive Officer Dietmar Kuhnt said he was sure the alliance would win a strong position in the German telecommunications market.

Veba will own 40 percent of O.TEL.O and RWE 37.5 percent. The remaining 22.5 percent made available by the withdrawal of Cable & Wireless will be held in trust by a bank while a new international partner is sought.

The new company already serves more than 2 million customers in Germany, including 700 large customers, over 500,000 mobile phone users -- on the E-plus network in which Veba owns 30 percent -- and 1.6 million cable TV subscribers.
